items.title: Dominic James "Nick" La Rocca Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The name 'Paren' appears only in the interviewer's reading of a letter from Don Fowler, quoting Louis Armstrong. The interviewee (Nick La Rocca) does not mention Paren, nor does he respond to the name specifically, only to the content of the letter regarding Louis Armstrong and the Dixieland band.

ctx.x: I mean Clarence Williams. You got me right that time because I'm making a mistake. I'm just telling you, I'm reading. I'm not reading. I'm telling you from my mind. Clarence Williams came to New York around 1923. The first white man he met on Broadway was me with an introduction from A.J. Perron, which you'll find in their books too. And this Negro is supposed to have her buddy bowling play. Now let me tell you about this man, who he is, where he come from. If any of you serious scholars doubt me, I was just…

All right. This is a letter dated May the 27th, 1958 from Don Fowler, 9441 Southwest 8th Drive, Portland 1, Oregon. It's to D. James, D. James, Nick LaRocca, at 2218 Constant Street, New Orleans, 13, Louisiana. And here's a paragraph that Mr. LaRocca would like for me to read. The other day I ran across an interesting statement by Louis Armstrong in his book, Satchmo. He is discussing his life in New Orleans in 1918, and this is a paragraph. Quote, One day when it was raining like mad, Daisy and I went in the…
Now read down where he says the other steel in the music of the Dixieland band, Louisiana Five.
